hub.legal: GRAVITAS is a free, fan-made companion for Elite Dangerous, made by Burak Servili (CMDR Hongark). It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Frontier Developments. It works only from what the game itself hands out: your Journal and status files, read on your own PC and never uploaded. It does not read the game's memory, change its files or hide anything. The map on gravitasmap.com shows public system data from Spansh. Elite Dangerous and Frontier are trademarks of Frontier Developments plc. Open source (MIT): github.com/Servly/gravitasmap
prof.note: Pick your ship from the list and save your window settings for it. GRAVITAS switches to them when you board that ship.

prof.custom: Or a name of your own
menu.w.defpos.d: Put this window back as GRAVITAS starts it: place, colour, when it shows, perspective, size, opacity and order
menu.claims.bonds.d: The game lists bonds in its Claims panel. They are never lost, not even when your ship is destroyed.
menu.claims.note.d: The report counts only that fight. Claims hold every bounty you have not cashed in yet. When they differ, the report says how much comes from before the fight.
menu.th.rec: GRAVITAS shows what the game writes about a Thargoid fight: threat level, kills and bonds, attacks, shutdowns, heat and your hull steps. The game writes no Thargoid hull, shield or hearts, so none are shown. While Thargoids are about, GRAVITAS also records the fight on your computer (the status file and the Journal events that matter). It starts at the first Thargoid sign and stops ten minutes after the last. Nothing is sent anywhere.

mode.debrief.name: Debrief
mode.debrief.desc: The ship keys you press, and a report of each fight.
tip.nav.debrief: Debrief mode: see the ship keys you press and how each fight went.
page.debrief.sub: See which ship keys you press and how a fight went, then look back at it. Move the windows in Edit HUD.
db.privacy: Debrief follows only the keys the game's own Bindings file gives to ship actions, and only while the game is in front, you are in your ship and no panel or menu is open. Nothing you type is seen, and nothing leaves this computer.
db.mode.on.d: Shows the ship keys you press while you fly, and keeps a record of each fight on this computer. Off until you turn it on.
tip.db.on: Turn Debrief on or off. When on, the input window shows while you fly and each fight is recorded here.
db.rules.on.d: Adds up to three plain facts from the log to a report. Preview: off until you have checked them against your own fights.
tip.db.rules: Show the facts the log supports at the end of a report. They describe what happened together, never advice.
menu.db.wnote: The input window shows while you fly with Debrief on. The report shows for a while after each fight. Move them in Edit HUD.
db.binds.note: Read from the game's Bindings file. A key used with Shift, Ctrl or Alt, or a button only on a joystick or pad, cannot be followed.
db.binds.none: No ship keys found in the Bindings file yet.
db.binds.else: Also on a joystick or pad (those presses are not seen):
db.past.note: Your last fights and hunts, with what you pressed (up to 30), kept on this computer only. Starred ones always stay.
tip.db.past.list: Your last debriefs. Pick one to read its timeline.
tip.db.past.show: Show this report on the game for a while.
db.g.l.hold: hold (a bar, its length is the time)
db.g.limits: The game writes no distance, aim, speed or heat level, so none is shown. Boost, chaff and heat sink show only as your own key presses. Enemy health appears only where a scan showed it.
mode.pvp.name: PVP
mode.pvp.desc: Record your fights against other commanders and look at them again.

pvp.privacy: PVP mode makes one file for each fight with another commander, from what the game writes about you. It holds no keys and no mouse data, and no commander ID. It is saved on this computer only. You send it to the other commander yourself, if you want to.
pvp.on.d: Records each fight with another commander as a file. Off until you turn it on.

pvp.shield: A shield going down ends a fight
pvp.shield.d: For fights that stop at the first shield down. Off: a fight ends at a death, a kill, a jump or after a calm.
tip.pvp.shield: End the fight when a shield goes down, yours or the other commander's (when scanned).
pvp.build: Put my ship's build in the file
pvp.build.d: The ship and its modules with their engineering, so you can compare builds. No ship name, no values.
tip.pvp.build: Add your ship's modules and engineering to the file. Turn off to keep your build to yourself.
tip.pvp.folder: Open the folder with your PVP files in Explorer.
pvp.where: Files: XXX_vs_YYY_fight_N.gravitas in %APPDATA%\com.gravitasmap.app\pvp\ (XXX is you, YYY the other commander, N the fight's number). Plain text you can open in any editor.
menu.pvp.wnote: The chip shows at the top while PVP mode is on. Move it in Edit HUD.
pvp.list.note: Your PVP fights, saved on this computer, newest first. Pick one to read its timeline.
pvp.next: To read your fight together with the other commander's, use the Compare tab.
tip.pvp.list: Your PVP fights. Pick one to read its timeline.
db.g.notproof: This is a record for learning, not proof: a file can be edited.
tip.pvp.tab.cmp: Put your fight and the other commander's side by side.
pvp.cmp.note: Load your fight files and the other commander's. GRAVITAS finds the fights that are the same fight, puts the two on one clock and shows them together. The files are only read here: nothing is sent anywhere.
tip.pvp.cmp.mine: Load all the PVP fights saved on this computer as yours.
tip.pvp.cmp.files: Pick one or more .gravitas files from your computer.
tip.pvp.cmp.clear: Forget the loaded files (nothing is deleted).
tip.pvp.cmp.list: The fights found in both sets of files. Pick one to read it.
pvp.cmp.nopair: No fight was found in both sets. Check that the files are from the same fight (the names and the times must match).
pvp.cmp.bad: {n} file(s) were not PVP fight files and were skipped.
pvp.cmp.nudge.d: If the two sides look out of step, move the other commander's side by hand (seconds).
tip.pvp.cmp.nudge: Shift the other commander's timeline to the left or right.
pvp.sync.death: Put on one clock by your death and their kill: that is one moment. The two PCs' clocks differed by {s} s.
pvp.sync.kill: Put on one clock by your kill and their death: that is one moment. The two PCs' clocks differed by {s} s.
pvp.sync.interdiction: Put on one clock by the interdiction both files wrote. The two PCs' clocks differed by {s} s.
pvp.sync.clock: No death, kill or interdiction to line the files up: the two PCs' clocks are used as they are. If the sides look out of step, move one by hand.

tip.dev.link: Get a one-time code (8 characters, valid for 2 minutes). Type it on gravitasmap.com in any browser and that browser shows and manages the same devices as this app.
tip.dev.linkcode: The one-time code. It works once and only for 2 minutes. Anyone who types it first gets the pairing, so keep it to yourself.

fb.title: Send feedback
fb.sub: Your message goes straight to the GRAVITAS developers. It is sent only when you press Send.
fb.kind.question: Question
tip.fb.kind: Tells us what kind of message this is.
fb.text: What would you like to tell us?
fb.text.ph: Example: when I open the Map page and press Show on the map, the window stays empty.
tip.fb.text: Write what happened or what you wish for. At most 4000 characters.
fb.shots.hint: Up to 3. You can also paste one with Ctrl+V.

tip.fb.remove: Takes this screenshot out of the message.
tip.fb.cmdr: So we know who wrote. You can leave it empty.
fb.mail: E-mail, if you want a reply (optional)
tip.fb.mail: Only used to answer you. You can leave it empty.
tip.fb.diag: Adds a short text of counts (no names, no Journal lines) that helps us find the cause.
fb.also: Always sent with the message: the app version and your Windows version. Nothing else.
fb.sent: Thank you! Your message was sent.
fb.fail.empty: Please write a few words first.
fb.fail.offline: Could not reach the server. Check your internet connection and try again.
fb.fail.big: The screenshots are too large. Please remove one.
fb.fail.other: The message could not be sent: {err}
vis.empty.p: Your travels appear here once you have flown in the game. GRAVITAS reads your Journals on this PC. Nothing is sent anywhere.
tip.vis.fx: Switch off glow, blur, parallax and the intro animation. Faster on a slow PC. Key X.
vis.search.ph: Where did I sell Gold?  Station, system, goods
tip.vis.search: Search your visits by system, station or goods. Key /.
tip.vis.chip: {name}: show only the stops where you did this (click again to clear).
tip.vis.fit: Fit all visits of this page into the view. Key F.
tip.vis.tilt: Tilt the map to see the height of the stops. Key T.
tip.vis.panel: Show or hide the details panel. Key C.
tip.vis.u.all: The last 12 months in detail. Older history is shown as faint dust.
tip.vis.timeline: Your whole history, one bar per month. Drag the window to look back in time, drag its edges to resize it, click an older month to open it. Wheel to zoom the window.
vis.lod.ind: Every stop shown · {n} on this page
vis.lod.grp: Grouped in {c} ly cells · {g} groups for {n} stops
vis.toast.slow: Drawing is slow on this PC.
tip.vis.ses: Open this play session as the page.
vis.act.none: Only passed through. No docking or trade here.
tip.vis.show: Open this system in the GRAVITAS MAP.
tip.vis.copy: Copy the system name, to paste it into the game's galaxy map search.
tip.vis.summary: Back to the summary of the page. Key Esc.
vis.keep.h: Keep a travel history on this PC
tip.vis.keep: Switch the travel history on or off. It stays on this PC and is never sent anywhere.
vis.keep.off: The travel history is off. When it is on, GRAVITAS reads your Journals and keeps a list of the systems you visited and what you did there, on this PC only. You can forget it again at any time.
tip.vis.forget: Delete the kept travel history from this PC. Your game Journals are not touched.
vis.forget.ask: Forget everything? This cannot be undone.
tip.vis.last: Type how many of your newest visits to show. Leave it empty to show all. Enter applies it.
tip.vis.last.apply: Show only this many of your newest visits.
vis.last.bad: Please enter a whole number from 1 to {max}.
prefs.autostart.d: Opens GRAVITAS in the tray when you sign in to Windows. The window stays hidden until you open it.
tip.prefs.autostart: Starts GRAVITAS by itself each time you sign in to Windows, in the tray.
prefs.autostart.fail: Windows did not allow this change.
prefs.mintray.d: The minimize button hides the window in the tray, by the clock. Off: it minimizes to the taskbar.
tip.prefs.mintray: Chooses where the window goes when you press minimize.
prefs.closetray: Keep running in the tray when closed
prefs.closetray.d: The close button hides the window and the game windows keep working. Off: closing quits GRAVITAS.
tip.prefs.closetray: Chooses whether the close button quits GRAVITAS or only hides its window.
prefs.data.note: Everything GRAVITAS keeps lives on this PC. The Journal folder belongs to the game and is only read.
tip.prefs.open: Opens this folder in Windows Explorer.
prefs.xfer.note: Save your settings to a file to move them to another PC, then load the file there. Phone pairing and values that belong to this PC are not included.
tip.prefs.export: Writes your settings into a file in your Documents folder and shows it.
tip.prefs.import: Reads a settings file made by GRAVITAS. Your current settings are kept as a copy first.
prefs.xfer.loaded: {n} settings loaded. Close GRAVITAS from the tray icon and open it again to apply them.
prefs.xfer.bad: That file is not a GRAVITAS settings file.
vis.loading.sub: Your travel history is built from the game's Journal files on this PC. The first time takes a moment.
tip.vis.backstop: Shows the stop you were looking at again.
tip.vis.u.year: One year per page. Older years open from the archive.
tip.vis.arch: An older period of your history, loaded from this PC. Only one old period is kept in memory at a time.
tip.vis.arch.x: Close the archive and go back to the last 12 months.
vis.arch.big: That period holds {n} stops. Please pick a shorter period.
vis.arch.err: Could not load {p} yet. Trying again.
vis.stat.detail: Showing the last 12 months in detail
vis.pg.alldetail: {n} stops in detail · older history as dust
vis.last.loaded: Only {max} stops are loaded. Pick an older period on the timeline to see more.
vis.sum.months: Added up from the monthly summaries. The top lists are approximate.
vis.ill: Spiral: illustration, not a star map
tip.vis.ill: The faint spiral behind the map is only decoration. Your stops, the route and the three landmarks (Sol, Colonia, Sagittarius A*) use real coordinates.
tip.w.front: Put this window in front of the others, where they overlap.
tip.w.back: Put this window behind the others, where they overlap.
kb.cap.title: Press the key you want to use
kb.cap.hint: Hold Ctrl, Shift or Alt, then press the key. Esc cancels.
kb.need.key: This key cannot be used. Try a letter, a digit, an F key or a number pad key.
kb.max: Use at most two modifier keys.
tip.kb.change: Press a new key for this job.
tip.kb.cancel: Close this window and keep the old key.
tip.tab.prefs.general: Language and the other general settings.
tip.kb.go: Open Settings > Key Bindings to set the keys.
tip.kb.back: Go back to the page you came from.
tip.tab.bgs: BGS Watch: your faction's influence from your own screenshots.
tip.act.claims_show: Shows your Claims total on the screen for a few seconds, worked out from your Journals the way the game's Claims panel counts it.
tip.act.claims_restore: Takes back every Claims reset and works Claims out again from your Journals (everything not cashed in since your last death), then shows the total.
theme.note: Choose the colours of the GRAVITAS window and of the menu over the game. The windows drawn over the game keep their own colours.
theme.custom.d: Pick any colour. The other tones follow it and the text stays easy to read.
theme.adjusted: Some tones were brightened so that the text stays easy to read.
tip.theme.set: Use the {name} colours in this window and in the menu.
tip.theme.custom: Pick a colour of your own. It changes at once and is saved when you let go.
tip.theme.reset: Go back to the GRAVITAS colours.
bgs.issue.no_pages: No page of the faction list was read.
bgs.issue.missing_page: A page of the list is missing: take it with F10 and scan again.
bgs.issue.row_count: A page shows another number of rows than expected: check that page.
bgs.issue.systems_count: The systems count on the page differs from the rows read.
bgs.issue.duplicate_page: A page was taken twice: the newer one is used.
bgs.issue.page_number_unread: A page number could not be read: the order of the screenshots is used.
bgs.issue.no_last_updated: LAST UPDATED could not be read: the time of the screenshot is used.
bgs.issue.not_sorted: The values are not sorted from high to low: the order check is off for this list.
bgs.issue.duplicate_name: Two rows have the same system name.
bgs.issue.names_unmatched: Some known systems did not appear in this list.
bgs.issue.systems_gone: Some systems of the last snapshot are not in this list.
bgs.state.snapped: Matched to a known name: please look
bgs.state.order: Breaks the high-to-low order: please check
bgs.state.jump: Changed a lot since the last snapshot: please check
bgs.err.not_list: This is not the Squadron > Faction list.
bgs.err.paste: Inara did not answer: paste the system names instead (one per line).
tip.bgs.scan: Reads the newest screenshots you took with F10 and proposes a table to confirm. Nothing is saved yet.
tip.bgs.names_fetch: Asks the public Inara page of your faction once for the system names. Only the names are kept.
tip.bgs.n: How many of the newest screenshots to read.
tip.bgs.window: Pages taken within this many minutes of each other become one snapshot.
tip.bgs.band: Your own target range, drawn in the charts. It is not a game rule: the game has no safe range. It only starts a retreat for a faction under 2.5 % and may start an expansion above 75 %.
tip.bgs.forget: Deletes every saved BGS snapshot and the list of system names from this PC.
tip.bgs.csv: Makes a CSV file of all saved snapshots for a spreadsheet.
page.bgs.sub: Your faction's influence in its systems, read from the screenshots you took yourself. Everything stays on this PC.
mode.bgs.name: BGS Watch
mode.bgs.desc: Influence of your faction in its systems, from your own F10 screenshots, with charts and a daily report.
tip.nav.bgs: BGS Watch: your faction's influence, charts and a daily report.
tip.bgs.tab.setup: Turn BGS Watch on, load the system names, read the screenshots and confirm the values.
tip.bgs.tab.today: What needs attention today, the biggest drops and gains, the tick estimate.
tip.bgs.tab.movers: Who moved since the comparison reading, and by how much.
tip.bgs.tab.risk: How close each system is to the edges of your band, and where it is heading.
tip.bgs.tab.heat: One column per snapshot, one row per system: the changes at a glance.
tip.bgs.tab.trends: A small chart for every system, all on the same scale.
tip.bgs.tab.fleet: All systems together: zones over time, median and spread.
tip.bgs.tab.tick: A rough estimate of when the tick happens, from your own snapshots.
tip.bgs.tab.report: A text block for Discord and CSV files.
bgs.on.d: Off by default. When on, you can read your F10 screenshots of the squadron faction list.
tip.bgs.on: Turns BGS Watch on or off. Nothing runs in the background: it reads only when you press the button.
bgs.on.note: It reads only the screenshots you took with F10 and the Journal. The images are never kept: only the numbers are saved on this PC.
bgs.names.intro: The reader checks what it reads against the list of your faction's systems. Load the list once.
tip.bgs.inara_id: Paste the address of your faction's Inara page (it contains minorfaction-presence and a number) or just the number. It is only used to open that page in your browser.
tip.bgs.inara_open: Opens that Inara page in your own browser. Without a number it opens the Inara home page, where you can search for your faction. GRAVITAS itself makes no request to Inara.
bgs.inara.steps: 1. Open your faction's Inara page (the list of its systems). 2. Press EXPORT at the end of the page. 3. Choose the downloaded CSV file here.
tip.bgs.names_csv: Loads the names of your faction's systems from the CSV you exported on Inara. Only the system names are kept.
bgs.inara.why: Why? Only to check the system names: the reader compares what it reads with this list, so a misread letter is corrected. GRAVITAS keeps only the system names from the file. The influence values and everything else in it are ignored and never saved. You only need to load it again when your faction gets more systems.
bgs.names.none: No system names yet. The first snapshot you save makes the list.
bgs.csv.fail: The file could not be read as the Inara CSV with a Star system column.
bgs.csv.big: The file is too large for a system list.
bgs.paste.h: Or paste the names, one per line:
bgs.paste.ph: Paste the names, one per line
tip.bgs.paste_save: Saves the pasted names as the list of known systems.
bgs.n.d: The newest N screenshots you took with F10 are read.
bgs.win.d: Pages taken within this time become one snapshot.
bgs.band.risk: Your target range is your own choice, not a game rule. The lower a value, the easier control is lost to another faction. Above 75 the faction may start an expansion.
bgs.jump: Warn when a value changes by more than
bgs.jump.d: points since the last snapshot. Such rows are marked for a look.
tip.bgs.jump: A value that jumps by more than this is marked so you look at it before saving.
bgs.dir: Screenshot folder (empty = the game's usual folder in Pictures)
tip.bgs.dir: Only needed when your screenshots are saved somewhere else. The files are only read, never changed.
bgs.export.fail: The CSV file could not be made.
bgs.forget.done: All BGS data was deleted ({n} files).
bgs.data.note: Only numbers are saved, in this app's own folder. The screenshots themselves are never copied or changed.
bgs.scan.fail: The screenshots could not be read.
bgs.scan.off: BGS Watch is off. Switch it on above.
bgs.scan.first: First snapshot: only the levels are known, so changes, trends and the tick appear from the second snapshot on. Take each page of Squadron > Faction with F10, then press the button.
bgs.scan.nonames: No system names loaded yet. That is fine: the first snapshot you save makes the list. Loading the Inara list (above) makes reading safer.
bgs.scan.nofiles: No screenshots were found. Take the pages with F10 in the game, then scan again.
bgs.scan.nodir: The screenshot folder was not found. Set it in Reading, above.
bgs.scan.noprop: The screenshots were found, but none of them is a page of the Squadron > Faction list.
tip.bgs.cf.pick: Several groups of screenshots were found. The newest is first.
tip.bgs.cf.acc: Marks every sure row as looked at. Unsure rows stay amber until you check them.
tip.bgs.cf.name: Click to type another name. Amber means the reader is not sure.
tip.bgs.cf.val: Click to type another value, for example 66.9.
tip.bgs.cf.alt: Other reading of the same cell. One click uses it.
bgs.cf.badval: That is not a value between 0 and 100.
tip.bgs.cf.ok: Say that you looked at this row and it is right.
tip.bgs.cf.save: Saves the numbers of this table as one snapshot on this PC. The pictures are not kept.
bgs.cf.blocked: This list cannot be saved yet: see the problems above.
bgs.cf.note: Only the numbers are saved. A cell you changed by hand counts as your own reading.
bgs.menu.note: The table to confirm and save the values is in the GRAVITAS window, on the BGS page.
bgs.menu.sum: Read {p} of {q} pages, {s} systems: {a} sure, {u} to check.
bgs.menu.open: Open the GRAVITAS window to confirm.
bgs.menu.open2: All rows are sure: open the GRAVITAS window to save.
bgs.e.off: BGS Watch is off. Turn it on in Setup.
bgs.e.none: No snapshots yet. Read your F10 screenshots in Setup and save the first one.
bgs.dq.utc: times in UTC, the game's clock; this PC's time is in the tips
tip.bgs.bar.minor: A change smaller than this is drawn pale, not bold. The game shows 0.1 steps. Kept only while this page is open.
tip.bgs.bar.tick: A tick is counted when at least this share of the systems changed between two snapshots. Kept only while this page is open.
tip.bgs.bar.base: Which earlier reading the change is measured against: the one before, about 24 h ago, the last reading of yesterday (UTC), or about 7 days ago.
tip.bgs.bar.show: Limits the history views (heat strip, trends, fleet).
bgs.accepted: accepted after a warning or typed by you
tip.bgs.na: No earlier reading to compare with (first snapshot).
tip.bgs.minor: Minor change: under {m} points, near the 0.1 step of the display.
tip.bgs.stale: Not in the newest snapshot: the value shown is the last one read.
tip.bgs.warncell: One or more of its cells were accepted after a warning or typed by you.
tip.bgs.save: Saves the first chart of this card as a PNG picture.
tip.bgs.find: Type part of a system name.
tip.bgs.z.low: Below your target range ({lo}): control is easier to lose.
tip.bgs.z.high: Above your target range ({hi}). Near 75 an expansion may start.
tip.bgs.incomplete: Incomplete snapshot: {n} rows were not read (a page was missing). Those cells are hatched, never zero.
tip.bgs.t.read: How many systems were read in the newest snapshot.
tip.bgs.t.up: Systems that went up since the comparison reading.
tip.bgs.t.dn: Systems that went down since the comparison reading.
tip.bgs.t.same: Systems with the same value as in the comparison reading.
tip.bgs.t.below: Systems below the low edge of your band.
tip.bgs.t.above: Systems above the high edge of your band.
bgs.att.none: Nothing needs attention with the current band.
bgs.att.note: Ranked by: outside your target range first, then an estimated crossing within about 6 days, then a run in one direction. The bar shows the value against your target range ({lo} to {hi}), the white tick is the comparison reading.
bgs.att.first: only the level is known, so only systems already outside the band appear. Change, trend and tick need more snapshots.
bgs.next.h: What you will see after the next snapshots
bgs.next.t: Change since last time, the biggest drops and gains, a trend for each system and the tick estimate. Nothing is guessed from one reading.
bgs.drops.q: Where did we lose the most since {b}?
bgs.gains.q: Where did we gain the most?
bgs.mv.need: Needs a second snapshot. A single reading has no before and after.
bgs.mv.q: Who moved, and by how much?
bgs.mv.note: Green bold = up, red bold = down. Pale = minor (under {m}, the game shows 0.1 steps). Grey = no change.
bgs.s.name: A to Z
bgs.band.label: band {lo} to {hi}
bgs.sl.q: How big were the biggest moves, against the band?
bgs.sl.note: Only the 8 biggest drops and 8 biggest gains (minor changes left out). A steep line is a big move. Click a line to open the system.
bgs.risk.q: Which systems are close to an edge, and are they heading there?
bgs.risk.note: Sorted by the distance to the nearest edge of your target range ({lo} or {hi}). Below the low edge control is easier to lose, above the high edge you are outside your range. The trend is the median slope of readings at least 20 h apart, with the middle half of the slopes in brackets. It is a straight-line estimate, not a forecast of the game. It needs 4 readings over 3 days.
tip.bgs.room: Distance to the nearest edge of your band ({lo} or {hi}). The arrow says which one.
tip.bgs.trendneed: A trend needs 4 readings over at least 3 days.
bgs.r.back: about {d} d back to the band
bgs.tr.need: Needs a second snapshot to draw a line.
bgs.tr.q: How is each system doing over time?
bgs.tr.q2: Which systems drift, and which are stable?
bgs.tr.note: Every tile shares one vertical scale ({a} to {b}) and one time axis, so lines can be compared by eye. Shaded = the band, dashed lines = its edges. Dots are real readings, a hollow amber dot was accepted after a warning or typed. A gap in a line is a snapshot where the system was not read, nothing is drawn between.
tip.bgs.seg.msort.name: Sort by name.
tip.bgs.seg.rfilter.low: Only systems below the low edge.
tip.bgs.seg.rfilter.risk: Systems inside the band that are close to an edge or heading there.
tip.bgs.seg.rfilter.high: Only systems above the high edge.
tip.bgs.seg.tsort.vol: Systems with the biggest typical step first.
tip.bgs.seg.tsort.name: Sort by name.
bgs.heat.need: Needs a second snapshot. With one reading there is no change to colour.
bgs.heat.q0: Which systems keep moving, day after day?
bgs.heat.q: Which systems keep moving, and when did each one start to slip?
bgs.heat.note: One column per snapshot, true order, with a break mark where more than 36 h passed. A column with an exclamation mark is an incomplete snapshot: its missing rows are hatched, never filled in. When a system has no value in the column before, the change is measured from the last reading and the tip says so.
tip.bgs.seg.hmode.chg: Colour by the change since the column before.
tip.bgs.seg.hmode.lvl: Colour by the level against your band.
tip.bgs.seg.hsort.move: Biggest drop since the comparison first.
tip.bgs.seg.hsort.vol: Systems with the biggest typical step first.
tip.bgs.seg.hsort.name: Sort by name.
bgs.fleet.one: First snapshot: {lo} below the band, {i} in it, {hi} above. Zones over time need more snapshots.
bgs.fm.one: Median influence {m}. A line needs a second snapshot.
bgs.fm.t: Median influence {m} ({d} vs previous). Below the band: {lo} ({dl}), above: {hi}.
bgs.zot.q: How many systems are in each zone, snapshot by snapshot?
bgs.zot.note: Counts are of the systems actually read in each snapshot (an incomplete one has fewer). Bars are equally spaced, the day of the month is under each one.
bgs.med.q: Is the faction as a whole gaining or losing?
bgs.med.note: Line = median of the systems read, shaded = the middle half of them (25th to 75th percentile). Needs no model, just the readings.
bgs.hist.h2: Distribution now against the previous complete snapshot
bgs.hist.q: How are the systems spread against the band?
bgs.hist.note: Bars = now, white dashed outline = the previous complete snapshot, 2 points per bar.
bgs.tick.one: With one snapshot the best help is to take one every hour around the time you expect the tick.
bgs.tick.need: Needs more data. Take a second snapshot and the interval that holds the tick appears.
bgs.tick.none: No tick seen yet: fewer than {pct} % of the systems changed in every interval.
bgs.tick.wide: A tick happened, but every interval is wider than 14 h. Take snapshots closer together, ideally one per hour around the expected time.
bgs.tick.win: The tick falls between {a} and {b} UTC (est., from {n} tight intervals).
bgs.tick.rough: The intervals disagree, so the tick moved or the readings are too far apart. Midpoints run from {a} to {b} UTC (rough).
bgs.tick.drift: The tick can move by up to about 1 hour from one day to the next, every system ticks at its own time, and the game's panels can show a tick up to 12 hours late. One snapshot per hour makes the estimate sharper.
bgs.tick.mini: Estimate from your own readings. See the Tick tab.
tip.bgs.lv: Higher confidence needs three or more tight intervals that agree.
bgs.tick.h3: Share of systems that changed, per interval
bgs.tick.q3: In which gaps between snapshots did the tick happen?
bgs.tick.note1: A tick is when many systems change at once. Only systems read in both snapshots count.
bgs.tick.multi: more than 26 h: may hold two ticks
bgs.tick.l4: Under each bar: the day the interval ends and its length. An orange length means more than 26 h, so it may hold two ticks.
bgs.tick.q4: What time of day is it, roughly?
bgs.tick.in1: A tick is somewhere in here
bgs.tick.in2: A tick is in here, but the interval is too wide to use
bgs.tick.note2: Everything here is an estimate from your own snapshots: there is no server and no other source. Solid violet bars: a tick happened inside. Dark bars: quiet, so the tick was not there. Dashed orange: too wide to use. Pink band: the estimated window.
bgs.tick.note3: The window is where the tight tick intervals overlap, trimmed by quiet intervals of the last 7 days. If they do not overlap, the tick moved and the band becomes a rough range.
bgs.rep.q: What do I post for the squadron today?
tip.bgs.rep.att: Systems near or below the low edge of your range (BOOST FIRST) and near or above the high edge (ABOVE YOUR RANGE).
tip.bgs.rep.cross: Systems that crossed the low or the high edge since the comparison.
tip.bgs.rep.tick: The estimated tick window, or 'needs more data'.
tip.bgs.faction: Optional. It is written into the first line of the report. It is not saved when you close the app.
tip.bgs.copy: Copies the text block, ready to paste into Discord. The report is always in English.
tip.bgs.csvlong: One line for every system and snapshot, with the change and a flag.
tip.bgs.csvwide: One row per system, one column per snapshot.
bgs.rep.note: Fixed-width block, so the columns line up in Discord. Only fields the data supports are written: with one snapshot there is no change line, and without a trend nothing says how many days are left.
bgs.fd.hdr.d: faction name (if typed) and the date of the newest snapshot
bgs.fd.snap.d: time of the snapshot (UTC), the earlier one it is compared with and the gap
bgs.fd.cnt.d: systems read, up, down, same, median
bgs.fd.band.d: how many below, inside and above your band
bgs.fd.def.d: up to 8 systems near or below the low edge: value, change, name and the first reason
bgs.fd.thi.d: up to 5 systems near or above the high edge, same fields
bgs.fd.dg.d: up to 5 each, only changes of {m} or more
bgs.fd.cross.d: systems that fell below the low edge, rose above the high edge, or came back
bgs.fd.foot.d: reading precision, incomplete snapshot, cells accepted after a warning
bgs.dt.tick: Many systems changed in this gap ({p}%): a tick is somewhere here
bgs.dt.one: One reading so far. History starts with the next snapshot.
bgs.dt.note: Pink bands: gaps in which many systems changed (the tick). Dots are real readings. Hollow amber = accepted after a warning or typed. Dashed lines: the two edges of your band.
tip.bgs.cf.crop: The part of the screenshot this value was read from.
bgs.csv.no_column: This file has no "Star system" column: use the EXPORT button of the Inara faction presence page.
bgs.csv.empty: No system names were found in the file.
bgs.csv.hint: Open your faction's page on Inara in your browser, press EXPORT, then load the CSV here. Reload it only when the faction gets more systems.
bgs.state.disagree: The two readings of this value differ: please check
bgs.state.confusable: Two similar digits (6, 8, 9, 0, 3, 5) are close: please check
bgs.err.flagged_rows: Some rows are still marked uncertain: look at them, or accept them unchecked.
tip.bgs.learned: Use the digit and letter shapes learned from your corrections when reading. Turn off to read with the built-in shapes only.
tip.bgs.crop: What the reader saw in this cell on the screenshot. Shown only for cells it doubts, never saved.
bgs.inara.ph: Paste the page address, or just its number
bgs.inara.badid: No faction number was found in that text. Paste the address of your faction's Inara page.
tip.bgs.imp: Reads one or several CSV files that Export CSV wrote (for example from a friend who read the screenshots on his PC). Each snapshot is placed at the time it was read. You see a summary first and nothing is saved until you confirm.
bgs.imp.note: Import a CSV that Export CSV wrote, for example from a friend who read the screenshots on his PC. Each snapshot is placed at the time it was read. Rows the sender did not check stay marked.
bgs.imp.sum: Snapshots in the file: {n}. New: {a}. Already here: {s}. Rows that could not be used: {b}.
tip.bgs.imp_go: Saves the new snapshots from this file at the time they were read.
tip.bgs.imp_cancel: Closes this summary. Nothing is saved.
bgs.imp.done: {a} snapshots imported. They are placed at the time they were read.
bgs.imp.fail: This file could not be read as a GRAVITAS BGS export.
bgs.imp.done1: 1 snapshot imported. It is placed at the time it was read.
tip.bgs.tab.defend: The systems to act on first, with the reason for each. A system that is falling counts as much as one that is already low.
tip.bgs.tab.changes: What moved by a point or more since the comparison snapshot, before and after.
tip.bgs.tab.overview: All systems over time in one picture: each row is a system, each column a snapshot.
bgs.d.title: Systems that need attention: {n}
bgs.d.sub: Below {lo}: {a}. Falling toward it or close to it: {b}. Above {hi}: {c}.
bgs.d.none: Nothing needs attention right now: all {n} systems are inside {lo} to {hi} and none is falling fast.
bgs.d.how: Each row is one system. The filled dot is now, the open dot is the earlier reading, the shaded area is your target range.
bgs.r2.low_d: Below {lo} by {e}, down {d} since the comparison
bgs.r2.high_d: Above {hi} by {e}, up {d} since the comparison
bgs.c.title: Fell by {x} points or more: {n}. Rose by {x} or more: {m}. Compared with: {b}.
bgs.c.none: No system moved by {x} points or more compared with: {b}.
bgs.c.how: Each line is one system from its earlier value (left) to its value now (right). Amber lines fell, blue lines rose. The shaded area is your target range.
tip.bgs.more: Data quality and the two finer settings (the size of a minor change and the tick threshold).
tip.bgs.qchip: How many systems the newest snapshot has, and when its numbers are from (UTC). Open Details for more.
bgs.r2.expand: At {v}: above 75 an expansion may start (about 15 points are taken when it ends)
tip.bgs.tab.squad: How many systems are below, inside and above your target range, over time.
tip.bgs.tab.edit: A table of every saved snapshot where you can correct a value, a time, or delete a snapshot.
tip.bgs.search: Type a system name (or part of it) and press Enter to open its data: every reading with the time, its trend and when it last changed.
bgs.need2: This view needs two snapshots. Take the next one after the next tick, or import a CSV.
bgs.d.how2: Each group is one situation. Change compares with {b}. Hover a row for the time of its last change.
tip.bgs.g.close: Inside your target range ({lo} to {hi}) but close to one edge or moving toward it.
bgs.c.title2: {n} fell and {m} rose by {x} points or more since {b}
bgs.c.how2: Each bar is one system: to the left (red) it fell, to the right (green) it rose. Hover a bar for the two times.
bgs.o.title: {n} of {t} systems are outside your target range now
bgs.o.how: Each row is a system, each column a snapshot. A cell shows the change since the snapshot before: green rose, red fell, grey is under {m}. A column that lights up all the way down is a tick. Hover a cell for the time and value.
tip.bgs.t.top: The 12 systems that need attention most.
bgs.t.find: {n} systems, time span {d} d, one shared scale, your target range shaded
bgs.t.how: Each box is one system. The big dot is the latest reading (red or green by the last change). The dotted line is 75. Hover a dot for its time and value.
bgs.s.find: Now: {a} below, {b} inside, {c} above your target range (at the start: {fa}, {fb}, {fc})
bgs.s.how: Stacked counts per snapshot. Red at the bottom is below your range, amber on top is above it. Hover for the time and the counts.
bgs.ed.how: Columns A, B, C are snapshots (the time is under the letter), rows 0, 1, 2 are systems. Click a cell and type to correct it, Enter goes down, Tab goes right, Esc cancels, Delete clears a cell. You can paste a block from Excel. Click a time to correct it. Nothing is saved until Save, then every chart updates.
tip.bgs.ed.save: Saves every typed value and time, then updates all charts at once.
tip.bgs.ed.discard: Forgets everything you typed and shows the saved values again.
tip.bgs.ed.find: Shows only the rows whose system name contains this text.
tip.bgs.ed.time: The time (UTC) this snapshot's numbers are from. Click to correct it.
bgs.ed.unsure: The reader was not sure about this value, or it was accepted without a check.
bgs.ed.badval: A value is a number from 0 to 100 with at most one decimal, for example 63.7.
bgs.ed.saved: Changes saved: {n}. All charts are updated.
bgs.ed.fail: The change could not be saved.
bgs.ed.none: No saved snapshots yet. Import from screenshots or import a CSV first.
bgs.ed.pasted: Cells pasted: {n}. Save to keep them.
bgs.ed.pasted_bad: Cells pasted: {n}. Skipped because they were not values: {b}.
tip.bgs.res: Automatic: every snapshot is its own column while your data is under 10 days old, then one column per UTC day. Daily: always one column per day (the last snapshot of that day). Every snapshot: always one column each. Nothing is ever deleted.
bgs.tp.snaps: Snapshots that day: {n} (the last one is shown)
bgs.cf.same: Nothing changed since the last saved snapshot. Save it anyway?
tip.bgs.cf.same_go: Saves this reading even though every value equals the last saved snapshot.
